components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors

      title: Validation message

      required:

          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"

## What I did

The create-owner pipeline already had a `RequireUniqueHousehold` step that skips its duplicate check when `sharesHousehold=true` (allowing an owner at an address already used by a same-lastName owner). What was missing was the **`householdId`** — a stable shared identifier assigned to owners in the same household, and returned on the response. I added that:

1. **`openapi.yml`** — added a read-only `householdId` string field to the `Owner` response schema (so the generated `OwnerDto` gains `getHouseholdId()`/`setHouseholdId()`).

2. **`Household.java`** (new, in `rest/function/owner/`) — a small utility with:
   - `normalize(...)` — trim, collapse whitespace, lower-case (the household-identity comparison).
   - `id(lastName, address)` — a stable identifier derived from the normalized last name + address (first 8 bytes of SHA-256, upper-hex). Because it's a pure function of the household fields, every owner in the same household deterministically gets the **same** value, with no stored column or lookup needed.

3. **`OwnerMapper`** — mapped `householdId` in `toOwnerDto` via `Household.id(owner.getLastName(), owner.getAddress())`, so both `POST /api/owners` (201 body) and `GET /api/owners/{id}` expose it.

4. **`RequireUniqueHousehold`** — refactored to reuse `Household.normalize`, keeping the duplicate-detection notion of "same household" identical to what the identifier is derived from.

## Result

The acceptance test `coreJoinersShareHouseholdId` — which creates owner A, then B and C sharing A's last name and address with `sharesHousehold=true`, and asserts B and C return an identical, non-blank `householdId` — passes. Full suite: `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0`, `BUILD SUCCESS`.

One design note: because `householdId` is *derived* rather than stored, owner A (created without `sharesHousehold`) also returns the same `householdId` as B and C automatically — so "both get the same identifier" holds for every member of the household, not just the joiners.
